info.title: Projektor API
info.description: Generated from the operation registry (apps/api/src/operations). Every operation here is also an MCP tool with the same name as its operationId. Path parameters are positional: where two operations share a path shape, the spec uses one set of names for both.

post.summary: Post a coordination message to a channel so the agent fleet can communicate
post.description:
Post a coordination message to a channel so the agent fleet can communicate: the workspace (default when scope is omitted), an issue, or a project (readable only by members who can see that project). Returns {id, scope, createdAt}; pass verbose:true for the whole stored row.

Constraints: projectId is required when scope is "project"; projectId only applies when scope is "project" or omitted.

scope.description: Channel scope: "workspace" (default), "issue:<uuid>" / "issue:<ref like PROJ-42>" (or just the bare uuid/ref), "project:<key|uuid>", or "project" together with projectId. Every spelling of a channel names the same channel

projectId.description: Project key (e.g. PROJ) or UUID. Use with scope "project"; on its own it selects that project's channel

agentId.description: Agent session UUID posting the message (optional)

verbose.description: Return the whole stored row instead of {id, scope, createdAt} (default false)

get.summary: List coordination messages for a channel (workspace by default, an issue, or a project), newest first by default
get.description:
List coordination messages for a channel (workspace by default, an issue, or a project), newest first by default. Returns {items, next?}; pass next back as cursor. Rows omit workspaceId and null keys. Omitted keys are null/empty/false; pass verbose:true for the raw shape. See /projektor/agents/response-conventions/.

Constraints: projectId is required when scope is "project"; projectId only applies when scope is "project" or omitted.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Channel scope: "workspace" (default), "issue:<uuid>" / "issue:<ref like PROJ-42>" (or just the bare uuid/ref), "project:<key|uuid>", or "project" together with projectId. Every spelling of a channel names the same channel

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Project key (e.g. PROJ) or UUID. Use with scope "project"; on its own it selects that project's channel

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor: pass the previous page's `next` (MCP) or `nextCursor` (REST) unchanged

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max messages to return (1–100)

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: desc = newest first, asc = oldest first

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Unix seconds: only messages created at or after this time (rows' createdAt is in milliseconds)

parameters.name: verbose
parameters.description: Return the raw stored rows, including workspaceId and null keys (default false)

post.summary: Register an agent session, optionally linked to an issue
post.description: Register an agent session, optionally linked to an issue. Returns {id, name}; verbose:true returns the stored row.

issueId.description: Issue UUID or ref like PROJ-42, to link this session to (optional)

name.description: Display name for the agent session (max 200)

kind.description: Deprecated, ignored (PROJ-336): self-declared session kind drives no behavior and is not returned.

verbose.description: Return the raw stored rows instead of the slim shape (default false)

get.summary: List agent sessions in the workspace, optionally filtered by issue or project
get.description: List agent sessions in the workspace, optionally filtered by issue or project. An ended session is never returned. Live entries only by default — a session that has stopped heartbeating is also excluded; pass includeStale:true to include those too. Each entry carries a `live` flag (false when its heartbeat has gone stale) and, when tied to an issue, that issue's ref (e.g. "PROJ-857") as issueRef. Rows are {id, name, issueRef?, live, startedAt, lastHeartbeatAt}; verbose:true returns the raw rows.

parameters.name: issueId
parameters.description: Filter by issue UUID or ref like PROJ-42 (optional)

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Filter to sessions linked to an issue in this project — UUID or project key. A session with no issue link is excluded when this is given (optional)

parameters.name: includeStale
parameters.description: Include active sessions that have stopped heartbeating (default: false — live entries only). Never includes ended sessions.

parameters.name: verbose
parameters.description: Return the raw stored rows instead of the slim shape (default false)

post.summary: Optionally transition an issue (completion-report rules apply, same as update_issue), then release every claim/lease the session holds and…
post.description: Optionally transition an issue (completion-report rules apply, same as update_issue), then release every claim/lease the session holds and end it — replaces update_issue + release_issue + release_files + end_agent. completionReport.remainder on a done transition creates a linked follow-up issue; its ref comes back as followUp.ref. A completionReport needs a status that moves the issue to in_review/done (or an issue already there); otherwise the call fails before anything changes, so the session stays live to retry. Returns {sessionId, issueRef, status?, followUp?}; verbose:true returns the ended session row.

issue.description: Issue UUID or ref like PROJ-42, to optionally transition

completionReport.description: Completion report, required by the review gate in the same cases update_issue requires it (optional). Shape: {summary, verification, prLink?, remainder?} — summary and verification are required.

remainder.description: What is NOT done. Only acted on in the call that moves the issue to done (ignored for in_review/other updates; it is still recorded in the report comment). When it is, a follow-up issue is created under the same parent with the same labels, linked follows_from this one; its ref is returned as followUp.ref

verbose.description: Return the raw stored rows instead of the slim shape (default false)

post.summary: Register an agent session and claim an issue (plus files, if given) in one call
post.description: Register an agent session and claim an issue (plus files, if given) in one call — replaces register_agent + claim_issue + claim_files + post_message. All-or-nothing with compensating cleanup: on any conflict (same errors as claim_issue/claim_files) the session is ended and nothing is left claimed. If the process crashes mid-call, the same claims become reclaimable once the session's heartbeat goes stale (120s). Returns {sessionId, leaseId, paths, issue}, with issue in get_issue's default shape, so no separate get_issue is needed; verbose:true returns the raw rows.

issue.description: Issue UUID or ref like PROJ-42, to claim

paths.description: File paths to claim alongside the issue (optional)

name.description: Display name for the agent session (max 200)

verbose.description: Return the raw stored rows instead of the slim shape (default false)

post.summary: Claim one or more repo file paths for an issue so the parallel fleet can see what is taken
post.description: Claim one or more repo file paths for an issue so the parallel fleet can see what is taken. Returns {created, overridden, reclaimed}, each a list of {path, agentId, claimedAt, expiresAt?}; expiresAt is set only on an agentless claim, which lapses after its TTL. Omitted keys are null/empty/false; pass verbose:true for the raw shape. See /projektor/agents/response-conventions/.

agentId.description: Agent session UUID claiming the files (optional)

get.summary: List active file claims in the workspace, optionally filtered by issue, path or project
get.description: List active file claims in the workspace, optionally filtered by issue, path or project. Live entries only by default — a claim whose holder has ended, stopped heartbeating, or (for an agentless claim) sat past its TTL is excluded; pass includeStale:true for all. Returns {items} of {path, agentId, issueRef, claimedAt, expiresAt?}; expiresAt is set only on an agentless claim, and stale:true marks a reclaimable claim (only possible with includeStale:true). Omitted keys are null/empty/false; pass verbose:true for the raw shape. See /projektor/agents/response-conventions/.

parameters.name: issueId
parameters.description: Filter by issue UUID or ref like PROJ-42 (optional)

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Filter by exact file path — shows who holds this file across issues (optional)

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Filter to claims on issues in this project — UUID or project key (optional)

parameters.name: includeStale
parameters.description: Include claims whose holder has ended, gone stale, or (agentless) passed its TTL (default: false — live entries only)

parameters.name: verbose
parameters.description: Return the raw stored rows instead of the slim shape (default false)

post.summary: Release file claims
post.description: Release file claims. With paths: releases those paths (optionally only those held by an issue). Without paths it releases everything held by agentId; else, with only issueId, the caller's claims on that issue; else everything held by the credential's single agent session (several live sessions: pass agentId). Returns {released: n, paths: [...]}.

paths.description: File paths to release; omit to release by agentId / issueId / session

issueId.description: Restrict release to claims held by this issue, UUID or ref like PROJ-42 (optional)

agentId.description: Agent session UUID, or the session name given to register_agent/start_work, whose claims to release when paths is omitted (optional)

get.description: List active issue leases in the workspace, optionally filtered by issue, agent or project. Each entry carries the linked issue's ref (e.g. "PROJ-857") as issueRef, and a `live` flag (false when the holder stopped heartbeating and the lease is reclaimable — only possible with includeStale:true). get.summary: List issues in the workspace, optionally filtered by status, priority, project, or assignee
get.description: List issues in the workspace, optionally filtered by status, priority, project, or assignee. Items are summary rows {ref,title,status,priority,type?,parent?,assignee?,updated,rollup?} by default; view:"full" returns every non-empty field. Items omit `body` by default — pass bodyChars:N (max 1000) for a preview, or includeBody:true for whole bodies. Pass includeRollups:true to attach a `rollup` (child status counts: total/byStatus/done/remaining) to each item (a zero rollup is omitted unless verbose:true). Omitted keys are null/empty/false; pass verbose:true for the raw shape. See /projektor/agents/response-conventions/.

post.summary: Create a new issue in a project
post.description: Create a new issue in a project. For an issue an agent should be able to pick up autonomously, the body should state acceptance criteria and scope (files/components) — see get_workflow's definition of ready. get_prioritized_issues excludes issues missing these by default. Verification isn't part of the readiness bar (PROJ-738) — it's required later, in the completionReport when entering review/done. Filing work you already finished? Create it straight in done with completionReport (and agentSessionId), and add `comment` and `links` in the same call instead of follow-up update_issue / add_comment / create_issue_link calls; everything commits together.

typeId.description: UUID of the task type to assign

completionReport.description: Only with a status of in_review or done. Shape: {summary, verification, prLink?, remainder?}. Same evidence rules as update_issue: unverifiable evidence from an agent sets needsAudit:true

remainder.description: What is NOT done. Only acted on in the call that moves the issue to done (ignored for in_review/other updates; it is still recorded in the report comment). When it is, a follow-up issue is created under the same parent with the same labels, linked follows_from this one; its ref is returned as followUp.ref

get.summary: Fetch up to 50 issues in one call, by ref (e.g
get.description:
Fetch up to 50 issues in one call, by ref (e.g. PROJ-42) and/or id. Cheaper than repeated get_issue calls for triage. Items carry customFields but no rollup/links/assignee_name, and omit `body` unless includeBody:true. Returned in the order refs/ids were given; `missing` lists (once each) any requested ref/id that didn't resolve or isn't visible to you. Omitted keys are null/empty/false; pass verbose:true for the raw shape. See /projektor/agents/response-conventions/.

Constraints: Provide refs or ids; At most 50 issues per call (refs + ids combined).

parameters.description: Include each issue's `body` (omitted by default)

post.summary: Create up to 50 issues in one project in one call
post.description: Create up to 50 issues in one project in one call. Each item takes create_issue's fields (including completionReport, comment and links). Returns `results` in item order: {ref, id, ...} for a created issue, or {error: {code, message}} for an item that was rejected (e.g. a bad link target or parent). A rejected item doesn't stop the others; the created ones commit together. A malformed item (wrong field type) rejects the whole call before anything is written, and so does a commit that fails because a referenced record (e.g. a status) was deleted mid-call.

get.summary: Return open issues ranked by a composite score
get.description: Return open issues ranked by a composite score: link-network centrality (in-degree) + priority + inverse story points. Useful for deciding what to work on next. By default, issues that fail the definition-of-ready check (missing acceptance criteria or scope/files) are excluded. If none of the open issues pass, the ranked (not-ready) list is returned anyway with `degraded: true` on the response and `needsGrooming`/`missingCriteria` on each issue, rather than an empty array — empty otherwise means "no open work", which would be a lie. Each issue is {ref,title,status,priority,score,needsGrooming?,missingCriteria?}; pass verbose:true for ids and the score breakdown.

patch.description:
Update an issue — status, priority, title, body, assignee, or labels. Review gating: pass agentSessionId to identify yourself as an agent; entering in_review as an agent requires completionReport. Agents CAN transition directly to done (no human approval gate) — but if the completionReport.verification isn't externally checkable (no CI run/PR/commit link), the issue is flagged needsAudit:true for after-the-fact human review. If the work is only partly done, pass completionReport.remainder when marking done: a follow-up issue (same parent and labels, linked follows_from) is created and its ref returned as followUp.ref.

Constraints: body cannot be combined with appendBody or bodyEdits; Nothing to update (use add_comment for a comment alone).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: UUID of the issue, or a ref like PROJ-42

appendBody.description: Text to add to the end of the current body (joined with a blank line). Not with `body`

bodyEdits.description: Find/replace edits applied to the current body in order; each `find` must match exactly once, or nothing is written. Not with `body`

statusId.description: UUID of the task status (null to clear)

parentId.description: Set or clear the parent issue — UUID or ref like PROJ-42 (null to remove)

customFields.description: Custom field values keyed by field key (see list_custom_field_defs)

agentSessionId.description: Your agent session id (from register_agent) — identifies this update as agent-initiated

completionReport.description: Required when an agent moves an issue into in_review; also gates the done transition. Shape: {summary, verification, prLink?, remainder?} — summary and verification are required.

post.description:
Create a new wiki page. `content` may start with an optional YAML frontmatter block (`---
type: runbook
tags: [foo]
status: draft
---
...`) — type (freeform; well-known values runbook|adr|spec|note), tags[], status (draft|current|stale|deprecated), verified_at, verified_by, owners[], verify_interval (days), template (boolean) are parsed and denormalised for filtering. Invalid frontmatter (bad status/enum, wrong type, unrecognised key) is rejected with a structured error, not ignored. Alternatively, pass `templateSlug` (from list_wiki_templates) to seed this page's content from an existing template page — its `template: true` flag is stripped from the seeded content (the new page is not itself a template). `templateSlug` and `content` are mutually exclusive; a `templateSlug` that doesn't resolve to a page flagged template:true is rejected. Returns the page's id, slug and url, and revisionId: null (a new page has no revisions; pass null as the first edit's baseRevisionId).

put.summary: Update a wiki page by id or slug (saves a revision when content changes)
put.description: Update a wiki page by id or slug (saves a revision when content changes). Pass baseRevisionId (the revisionId get_wiki_page returns, or the one this tool or patch_wiki_page returned for your last edit; null if the page has never been revised) for conflict-safe writes: if the page advanced since baseRevisionId, the write is rejected with a structured conflict (currentRevisionId + a unified diff) instead of silently overwriting. Omitting baseRevisionId is DEPRECATED — it keeps today's last-write-wins behavior during the transition and will be rejected in a future version. The revision pointer only advances on content edits, so baseRevisionId doesn't cover title/slug/parentId-only changes; those are last-write-wins against writes that finished before your call, but any write that lands while your call is in flight returns a 409. `content` may include a YAML frontmatter block (see create_wiki_page); it's re-parsed on every content edit, replacing the page's previously-stored metadata. Omitting `content` leaves the page's existing frontmatter metadata unchanged. Returns {ok, url, revisionId}; pass revisionId as the next edit's baseRevisionId.

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: Page slug (alternative to id)

content.description: Markdown content, optionally starting with a YAML frontmatter block

parentId.description: Parent page ID (null to unset parent, omit to leave unchanged)

newSlug.description: Rename the page's slug; the old slug becomes a redirect so existing links keep resolving

baseRevisionId.description: Deprecated if omitted (see tool description). The revision id this edit is based on — null if the page has never been revised.

summary.description: Optional edit message/changelog note, recorded on the created revision

patch.summary: Section-addressed patch operations on a wiki page's markdown, by id or slug
patch.description: Section-addressed patch operations on a wiki page's markdown, by id or slug. Sections are addressed by heading text, with or without the leading `#` markers (a `#`..`######` line and everything up to the next heading; `#` lines inside fenced code blocks or the YAML frontmatter block are not headings). A heading that appears more than once on the page is ambiguous and rejected — patch targets must be unique. Ops: append_to_section (add text at the end of the section's body), replace_section (replace the section's body, heading kept), insert_after_heading (insert text directly under the heading, before the existing body), append_to_page (append at the very end of the document, no heading needed), set_frontmatter (merge `values` into the page's YAML frontmatter block without touching the rest of the content — a key set to null is removed; a page with no frontmatter block gains one). baseRevisionId is required for every op except append_to_page (the revisionId get_wiki_page returns, or the one your last update/patch returned; null if never revised) — conflict detection is SECTION-scoped, not whole-page: two agents patching different sections never conflict, even if the page's revision advanced between their reads — only the SAME section changing underneath the caller conflicts (append_to_page and set_frontmatter skip this check; baseRevisionId is only validated as belonging to the page). A heading miss (never existed, or deleted/renamed since baseRevisionId) returns the page's current headings so a caller can retry against reality. Returns {ok, url, revisionId}; pass revisionId as the next edit's baseRevisionId. Creates a revision like update_wiki_page; ops other than set_frontmatter leave frontmatter metadata untouched beyond reparsing it (never stamps verified_at).

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: Page slug (alternative to id)

heading.description: Target section's heading text (required for append_to_section, replace_section, insert_after_heading)

text.description: Text to add/replace (required for every op except set_frontmatter)

values.description: set_frontmatter only: frontmatter keys to set (type, tags, status, verified_at, verified_by, owners, verify_interval, template). A key set to null is removed from the page's frontmatter.

baseRevisionId.description: The revision id this patch is based on — null if the page has never been revised. Required except for append_to_page.

summary.description: Optional edit message/changelog note, recorded on the created revision
